citation.title: Optimization of 3D controlled ELM-free state with recovered global confinement for KSTAR with n = 1 resonant magnetic field perturbation
citation.authors: S.K. Kim, R. Shousha, S.H. Hahn, A.O. Nelson, J. Wai, S.M. Yang, J.-K. Park, R. Nazikian, N.C. Logan, Y.M. Jeon, Y. In, J.H. Lee, J. Kim, C.Y. Lee, Y.-S. Na, E. Kolemen

topic: Adaptive real-time n=1 RMP amplitude control on KSTAR. The paper reports carbon-impurity CES Ti pedestal dynamics and BES/ECEI edge fluctuations.
own_question: Can Dα-based adaptive RMP control keep ELM suppression while recovering confinement? What role does Ti pedestal widening play?
actual_method_and_evidence: This is a single main discharge (#26004), with one comparison locking shot (#26014). The real-time controller used Dα-derived ELM frequency only. CES data for C6+ impurities were averaged over 100 ms and fitted offline with tanh functions. The analysis also includes offline stability calculations (EPED/MISHKA), transport analysis (ASTRA/NCLASS), and linear CGYRO runs. BES/ECEI coherence was analyzed offline. In this discharge, the authors report that fluctuations rose at ELM-suppression onset, coincident with Ti pedestal widening, and were insensitive to RMP amplitude. No figures were visually checked.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: In one KSTAR RMP discharge, the carbon-impurity CES Ti pedestal is reported to respond differently to RMP amplitude during the degradation and recovery phases. The reported response was larger in the recovery phase. This makes pedestal-top impurity Ti a dynamically relevant quantity during ELM control.
claim_checks.qualification: The measurement is impurity (C6+) Ti, not main-ion Ti, and comes from a single discharge. Profiles were 100 ms averaged and fitted offline; Ti was not used as a real-time input. The authors' interpretation is hysteresis.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: The authors report that BES/ECEI edge fluctuation coherence near ψN~0.96 coincided in time with ELM-suppressed phases and with Ti pedestal broadening. They interpret this as supporting a turbulence-driven increase in ion heat diffusivity.
claim_checks.qualification: The link is correlational and from offline spectral analysis. The mechanism is the authors' interpretation, supported only by linear gyrokinetic runs. Fluctuations measured are electron-channel quantities (δTe, δne), not ion quantities.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The only real-time input was Dα ELM frequency. CES timing is given as 100 ms averaging only; CES report arrival latency is not stated and remains unknown. BES/ECEI were used offline only.
validation_if_relevant: There is no predictive validation and no data split; this is an experimental case study.
forbidden_inferences: That a Ti nowcast was used or needed in the control loop
Generality beyond #26004 or to KSTAR2022 data
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as motivation that pedestal impurity Ti evolves on control-relevant timescales and co-varies with edge BES/ECEI fluctuations under RMP. Do not cite it as nowcasting precedent.
